panels.title: Request rate (status class)
panels.description: Request rate of the merged S3 app collapsed into HTTP status classes (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx), one line each — the at-a-glance health shape. Since the 2026-08 gateway/api merge there is a single app, so no handler filter is applied. Requests rejected by the outer middlewares (auth/ACL/validation/read-only/fs-pressure) are not counted here — the metrics middleware sits inside them; pressure sheds appear on the fs_cache_shed panel.
Object payload bytes recorded by the GET handler at response creation — intended transfer size, not wire bytes (client aborts still count in full; HEAD/LIST/error bodies not counted).
panels.title: Egress (download throughput)

panels.description: Object payload bytes recorded on SUCCESSFUL put_object/upload_part — not wire bytes (failed/aborted uploads count zero; UploadPartCopy counts as upload despite no client ingress).
panels.title: Ingress (upload throughput)
Redis memory (redis-queues cluster)
panels.description: Memory of the redis-queues CLUSTER (noeviction) — the instance that carries the upload LPUSH, chunk pub/sub and cephor:* coordination keys; when it fills, every write fails. Emitted by the app collector, which sums used_memory/maxmemory across all cluster primaries (a RedisCluster INFO returns one dict per node). max() de-dupes the identical value each pod reports; pods that cannot reach the cluster report 0 and are ignored by max().

panels.title: Cache disk usage (PVC quota)
panels.description: statvfs on the cache mount = the CephFS PVC QUOTA, not the backing pool. The two diverge sharply when the pool fills ahead of the quota (the 2026-07-24 blind spot) — pool fullness lives on the Ceph dashboard, not here.

panels.title: Cache parts on disk
panels.description: Census from the last COMPLETED GC phase. The raw gauge starts at 0 on every janitor restart and stays there until the next sweep finishes, which is why this read 0 for hours at a time; max_over_time([6h]) carries the last real census across those gaps. A sustained 0 over a full 6h window means no sweep has completed — check 'Janitor cycle health'.

panels.title: Janitor cycle health
panels.description: Seconds since the last COMPLETED janitor cycle (-1 = none since start). A line climbing without resetting means a phase is stuck and every census gauge on this dashboard is stale.

panels.title: Cache age distribution
panels.description: Census from the last COMPLETED GC phase — see 'Janitor cycle health'. All-zero with a non-zero cache disk means the phase has not finished.

panels.title: Ready replicas
panels.description: Ready replicas per Deployment. The `api` Deployment is excluded: the internal API now runs as the api-local DaemonSet, so the Deployment sits at 0 replicas and only added a permanent red 0 to this panel. DaemonSets are not covered by this metric.

panels.title: Abandoned-part reclaim (janitor)
panels.description: Terminally-abandoned parts reclaimed by the janitor. Was querying fs_janitor_abandoned_reclaimed_total, which is not a metric this codebase emits (panel was permanently empty); the real signal is the abandoned reason on fs_janitor_deleted_total.

panels.title: Read tiers served
panels.description: The whole point of the read tier. `local` should climb as retention fills each node's shard and `pool` should fall. All traffic collapsing back onto `pool` means retention, promotion or peer fetch has silently stopped working.

panels.title: Peer fetches declined
panels.description: server_busy is real contention at the peer. client_cap is this pod's own per-peer cap — if it rises while server_busy stays flat, readers are shedding their own prefetch window and HIPPIUS_PEER_FETCH_MAX_INFLIGHT is below HTTP_STREAM_PREFETCH_CHUNKS.

panels.title: Promotion skipped (disk pressure)
panels.description: Promotion backpressure must engage BEFORE the PUT-refusal gate: this should start rising while fs_cache_shed is still flat at zero. Both flat while free space falls means the gate is not engaging.

panels.title: SSD cache vs free (per node)
panels.description: Retained read tier against remaining headroom. cache should rise and plateau under the evictor's floor; cache pinned at the disk size with free flat is eviction failing to keep up.

panels.title: Eviction rate
panels.description: Byte rate is the one that matters: prod's part p50 is 686 bytes, so a part-count page is almost uncorrelated with space reclaimed.

panels.title: Eviction invariant breach (must stay 0)
panels.description: ALERT-WORTHY, not log-worthy. Any non-zero value means the eviction worklist and the only-evict-replicated durability invariant have diverged — the evictor was offered a part whose SSD copy may be the only durable one.

panels.title: SSD scan cost (F1 regression guard)
panels.description: Retention grew the SSD tree from the undrained backlog to the node's entire replicated shard (2.28M parts on prod). Watch duration against the worker's poll interval — a scan approaching its own period is the walk eating the node.

panels.title: Landed announcements
panels.description: The api->agent discovery fast path. Sustained dropped/s with recorded/s at zero is the wire contract broken between landed.py and landed.rs — discovery silently falls back to the reconciler walk.

panels.title: Read-recency writes
panels.description: A DB UPDATE on the read path, sampled to one per part per window. The sampler stops absorbing when a scan touches more distinct parts than its memo holds — which is exactly the full-shard read this tier exists for — so watch this against Postgres write load.
